catalogueTitle: "Can I travel with the other speakers?"
demoRole: Cross-traveller reasoning, shared programme context, correlated-risk constraints
note: Mei Ling Goh (ait-draft-30) asks that the Wanderpay delegation - herself, Siti Rahmah (ait-draft-11) and Arjun Rao (ait-draft-10, delegation lead, REQUIRED keynote speaker and moderator) - travel down together on the same KUL->SIN service, after planning floated splitting the group across the morning MN218 and the afternoon MN220. This triggers the policy clause criticalParticipantTransportConcentration: same-delegation travel-together request involving a programme-critical participant. The deterministic check flags that all three on MN218 concentrates the payments-keynote's only external speaker AND the payments-panel moderator + 2 of 3 panellists on one service; a same-day alternative (MN220) exists. Per the clause the operator proposes a split and discloses the trade-off; the travellers then EXPLICITLY instruct togetherness, which outranks the default only because disclosure happened first - the request is honoured with the reasoning and accepted risk recorded. Consistency cross-reference: scenario S1 (21 Sep) later retimes exactly this MN218 service and all three are affected together, demonstrating the flag was prescient; the S1 pack's baseline already encodes the togetherness outcome. Catalogue MVP boundary honoured: the correlated-risk constraint lives as a policy clause + machineHint in data (recorded in organiser-policy.json schemaGaps); no scenario-specific risk logic is added. expectedReasoningHooks: Cross-traveller / group reasoning: match 'the Wanderpay group' to roster drafts 10/11/30 and the SHARED_FLIGHT_GROUP dependency pattern; align three travellers' inventories against one service rather than processing three isolated requests.

Correlated-risk constraint from data: clauses.criticalParticipantTransportConcentration (trigger SAME_DELEGATION_CRITICAL_TRAVEL_TOGETHER_REQUEST). Deterministic flag: a single disruption of MN218 would strand the payments-keynote's only external speaker and the payments-panel moderator + 2 of 3 panellists; an alternative same-day service (MN220) exists, so the flag fires.

Clause mechanics: the group request is honoured UNLESS the flag fires; when it fires the operator proposes a split and records reasoning, discloses the trade-off, and the travellers' explicit instruction outranks the default only after disclosure. Here they choose togetherness -> honoured, with accepted risk recorded.

Arrival viability for both layouts: MN218 (07:25) and MN220 (15:20) both satisfy every member's buffer for their 1 Oct commitments (Arjun's 12h programme-critical buffer, Siti/Mei Ling's 6h standard); the decision is genuinely about correlated risk, not feasibility.

Inventory/fare alignment: MN218 and MN220 are same-carrier same-route at the same fare (SGD 98) - no fare difference either way, so the split proposal carries no cost argument; seating/baggage for the group is a soft preference, not a constraint.

Prescience cross-reference (data, not code): scenario S1 retimes MN218 on 21 Sep and all three are affected together - exactly the correlated outcome the flag anticipated. The pack never hardcodes this link; it is a documented expectation for the demo narrative.
